definitions.explanation: An equal split or balance between two sides, outcomes, or possibilities. Used to describe situations where neither side has an advantage.

examples.japanese: {勝|か}つ{確率|かくりつ}は{五分五分|ごぶごぶ}だ。
examples.english: The odds of winning are fifty-fifty.

examples.japanese: {両|りょう}チームの{実力|じつりょく}は{五分五分|ごぶごぶ}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think both teams are evenly matched.

examples.japanese: {手術|しゅじゅつ}が{成功|せいこう}するかどうかは{五分五分|ごぶごぶ}だと{医者|いしゃ}に{言|い}われた。
examples.english: The doctor told me the chances of the surgery succeeding were fifty-fifty.

notes:
An expression using {分|ぶ}, a traditional unit meaning one-tenth. Five-tenths plus five-tenths equals a whole, conveying the idea of a perfectly even split. Very commonly used in everyday conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {五分五分|ごぶごぶ}の{勝負|しょうぶ}: an even match
- {五分五分|ごぶごぶ}の{確率|かくりつ}: a fifty-fifty chance
- {五分五分|ごぶごぶ}の{戦|たたか}い: an evenly fought battle

USAGE:
Can be used as a noun ({五分五分|ごぶごぶ}だ) or as a modifier ({五分五分|ごぶごぶ}の). Often used when discussing the outcome of competitions, elections, medical procedures, or any situation with uncertain results.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {互角|ごかく}: evenly matched — emphasizes equal ability or strength between opponents
- {半々|はんはん}: half-and-half — used more for splitting things (costs, portions) rather than competition outcomes
- {拮抗|きっこう}: closely contested — more formal, often used in written language
